You are a helpful chemistry assistant. You build 3D molecular
  structures from the chemical information you are given, including 2D drawings
  supplied as images.

  When you are given a 2D drawing of a molecule, your task is to produce the 3D
  structure that drawing depicts and save it as `answer.xyz` in your working
  directory.

  Requirements for `answer.xyz`:
  - Include all explicit hydrogens.
  - Use a right-handed Cartesian coordinate system, units of angstroms.
  - Standard XYZ format: first line is the total atom count, second line a
    one-line comment, each remaining line `Element X Y Z`.

  When you are done, confirm that `answer.xyz` exists in the working directory.

A 2D structure of a molecule is provided as a PNG file in your working directory: mol_0008.png

Build the 3D structure it depicts and save it as answer.xyz.

im.crop((265,0,770,400)).resize((1515,1200)).save('crop.png')
PY

cat > build.py <<'PY'
from rdkit import Chem
from rdkit.Chem import AllChem
import numpy as np
# 2d image coordinates, x to the right, y upwards (Cartesian right-handed, z towards viewer)
positions={
0:(20,194),1:(80,90),2:(202,90),3:(263,195),4:(202,300),5:(80,299),
6:(392,218),7:(392,338),8:(495,398),9:(495,518),10:(391,579),11:(288,516),12:(597,338),13:(704,350),14:(756,458),15:(706,566),16:(597,218),17:(495,161),18:(298,143),19:(350,29),20:(703,160),21:(288,385),22:(470,57),23:(186,583),24:(589,593)}
# atom numbers 0-5 aryl ring, 6 a1,7 a2,8 a3,9 a4,10 a5,11 a6,12 a7,13 a8,14 a9,15 a10,16 a11,17 a12,18 a13,19 a14,20 a15,21 N1,22 N2,23 O carbonyl,24 O ether
rw=Chem.RWMol()
for i in range(25):
 sym='N' if i in (21,22) else 'O' if i in (23,24) else 'C'
 rw.AddAtom(Chem.Atom(sym))
B=Chem.BondType
edges=[(0,1,B.AROMATIC),(1,2,B.AROMATIC),(2,3,B.AROMATIC),(3,4,B.AROMATIC),(4,5,B.AROMATIC),(5,0,B.AROMATIC),
(3,6,B.SINGLE),(4,21,B.SINGLE),(6,7,B.SINGLE),(7,21,B.SINGLE),(21,11,B.SINGLE),(11,23,B.DOUBLE),(11,10,B.SINGLE),(10,9,B.SINGLE),(9,8,B.SINGLE),(8,7,B.SINGLE),(8,12,B.SINGLE),(12,16,B.SINGLE),(16,17,B.SINGLE),(17,6,B.SINGLE),(17,22,B.SINGLE),(22,19,B.SINGLE),(19,18,B.SINGLE),(18,6,B.SINGLE),(22,20,B.SINGLE),(20,13,B.SINGLE),(13,12,B.SINGLE),(13,14,B.DOUBLE),(14,15,B.SINGLE),(15,24,B.SINGLE),(24,9,B.SINGLE)]
for a,b,t in edges:rw.AddBond(a,b,t)
m=rw.GetMol();Chem.SanitizeMol(m);m=Chem.AddHs(m)
print(Chem.rdMolDescriptors.CalcMolFormula(m))
# calculate parity expected from XY arrangement and stereobond direction in the provided drawing
xyz=np.zeros((m.GetNumAtoms(),3))
for i,(x,y) in positions.items():xyz[i]=[x,-y,0]
# Explicit display H (7,8,9,12), stereo derived from respective drawn dash/wedge
hydrogen_places={7:(392,458,+105),8:(493,285,-105),9:(493,635,-105),12:(598,456,-105)}
for center,(x,y,z) in hydrogen_places.items():
 hs=[n.GetIdx() for n in m.GetAtomWithIdx(center).GetNeighbors() if n.GetAtomicNum()==1]
 assert len(hs)==1,(center,hs)
 xyz[hs[0]]=[x,-y,z]
# For position 6-18 wedge, and 17-22 wedge, z of terminal atom relative central vertex positive (towards viewer)
xyz[18,2]=105
xyz[22,2]=105
# center 17 explicit H (not shown) goes opposite to N wedge
h17=[n.GetIdx() for n in m.GetAtomWithIdx(17).GetNeighbors() if n.GetAtomicNum()==1][0]
xyz[h17]=[520,-144,-105]
# get parity reference from generic center in CCW (keep neighbor order: F Cl Br I)
toy=Chem.MolFromSmiles('F[C@](Cl)(Br)I');toy=Chem.AddHs(toy)
assert AllChem.EmbedMolecule(toy,randomSeed=11)==0
central=toy.GetAtomWithIdx(1);nv=[n.GetIdx() for n in central.GetNeighbors()];r=np.array(toy.GetConformer().GetPositions());v=r[nv]-r[1];ref=np.sign(np.linalg.det(np.stack((v[1]-v[0],v[2]-v[0],v[3]-v[0]))));print('ref',ref,central.GetChiralTag(),nv)
for j in [6,7,8,9,12,17]:
 at=m.GetAtomWithIdx(j);ids=[n.GetIdx() for n in at.GetNeighbors()];v=xyz[ids]-xyz[j]
 parity=np.sign(np.linalg.det(np.stack((v[1]-v[0],v[2]-v[0],v[3]-v[0]))))
 assert parity!=0,(j,ids,v)
 at.SetChiralTag(Chem.ChiralType.CHI_TETRAHEDRAL_CCW if parity==ref else Chem.ChiralType.CHI_TETRAHEDRAL_CW)
 print('center',j,'nbrs',ids,'parity',parity,'tag',at.GetChiralTag())
Chem.AssignStereochemistry(m,force=True,cleanIt=True)
print('isomeric SMILES',Chem.MolToSmiles(Chem.RemoveHs(m)))
print('CIPs',[(a.GetIdx(),a.GetProp('_CIPCode')) for a in m.GetAtoms() if a.HasProp('_CIPCode')])
# conformer search using MMFF and save low energy geometry
p=AllChem.ETKDGv3();p.randomSeed=182; p.numThreads=4; p.maxIterations=1000
ids=AllChem.EmbedMultipleConfs(m,numConfs=100,params=p)
print('Embedded',len(ids),flush=True)
props=AllChem.MMFFGetMoleculeProperties(m)
res=AllChem.MMFFOptimizeMoleculeConfs(m,numThreads=4,maxIters=600,mmffVariant='MMFF94s')
rank=sorted((energy,idx,status) for idx,(status,energy) in enumerate(res))
print('best conformers',rank[:12])
best=rank[0][1]
xyz3=m.GetConformer(best).GetPositions()
with open('answer.xyz','w') as f:
 f.write(f'{m.GetNumAtoms()}\nStrychnine, stereochemistry from mol_0008.png, RDKit MMFF94s minimized\n')
 for atom,(x,y,z) in zip(m.GetAtoms(),xyz3):f.write(f'{atom.GetSymbol()} {x:.8f} {y:.8f} {z:.8f}\n')
PY
python build.py
